human_tolerance.notes: Found in residential areas throughout its range and readily attracted to sunflower and safflower bird feeders; a study in Atlanta, Georgia found cardinals suppress West Nile virus after infection.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Two to four clutches a year, typically three or four eggs each; incubation takes 12 or 13 days and young fledge 10 or 11 days after hatching. The male forages while the female incubates, and may incubate briefly himself.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Both sexes are territorial and mark the territory with song throughout the year, so singing is not confined to the breeding season.

vocalizations.description: Clear, loud whistled song patterns repeated several times and then varied. Both sexes sing, the songs of the two sexes are not distinguishable to the human ear, and individuals learn their songs, so they vary regionally.
A short metallic chip, given when predators approach the nest and warning the female and nestlings.

conservation.note: Wikipedia's speciesbox gives the IUCN 3.1 status least concern.

range.note: Numerous across the eastern United States from the southern half of Maine to Minnesota to the Texas-Mexico border, and in southern Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick and Nova Scotia; recorded in Bermuda.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: It is a ground feeder and finds food while hopping on the ground through trees or shrubbery; it flies between song perches and glides between them.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in thick and dense shrubs, trees and vine tangles, built of twigs, grass and plant fibres in a cup 5.1-7.6 cm tall and 10.1 cm across; Cup chosen for that domed open cup.

traits.mass_kg.note: Wikipedia's stated average adult weight of 44.8 g.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 21-23.5 cm body length.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives no typical lifespan, only that annual adult survival is estimated at 60-65% and that the oldest wild bird banded lived at least 15 years and 9 months (28.5 years in captivity). 1.5 years is the median adult longevity implied by constant 62.5% annual survival: ln(0.5)/ln(0.625) = 1.47 years.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia gives the adult diet as mainly (up to 90%) weed seeds, grains and fruits, and adds snails and insects including beetles, cicadas and grasshoppers. The 90% figure is an upper bound, so the seed and fruit shares are set below it and the invertebrate share above zero; the split between seeds and fruits, and the monthly windows, are authored judgement.

traits.social.note: A territorial songbird: the male marks his territory with song and the female incubates while he forages, so birds are normally seen as a pair; the group size upper bound is authored judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Wikipedia describes daytime song from exposed song perches, nest watching and ground foraging by day, with no nocturnal behaviour; Diurnal is the judgement mapping.

traits.defense.note: Flies off and gives the metallic chip alarm call when a predator approaches the nest; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: bold and feeder-attracted in residential areas, shyer where it is hunted or handled.

habitat.use.note: The ground share follows Wikipedia's description of a ground feeder that hops through trees or shrubbery; the arboreal share covers nesting, song perches and flight.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the invertebrate window is judgement, tied to the fact that the young are fed almost entirely on insects; nesting and perch weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia records the species as found in residential areas throughout its range and attracted to feeders containing sunflower and safflower seeds, and cites a 2016 Atlanta, Georgia study on West Nile virus.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia gives no migration for this species and describes pairs holding territory year-round, with both sexes singing throughout the year.

seasonal.phases.note: Clutch size, clutch number, nest dimensions, incubation and fledging times from the Reproduction section; the month window for breeding is authored judgement, since the article gives no calendar dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The nestling period of 10 to 11 days is from Wikipedia; the rest of the 70-day juvenile duration, from fledging to independence, is authored judgement, as is the scale.

vocalizations.note: Song and alarm descriptions from Wikipedia's vocalisation section (clear repeated whistled patterns sung by both sexes, songs learned and regionally variable; short metallic chip at the nest). Time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement since no open source quantifies them.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description (brown above and red-brown below, with brick-coloured crest, forehead, wings and tail; the male's red comes from dietary carotenoids, and beaks are greyish-black until the final adult plumage in the fall). The crest and face-mask parts, proportions and palette slots are authored judgement to render the crest and mask that the description names.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag is 'seed' because Wikipedia calls it mainly granivorous and a ground feeder; flee_m is judgement, scaled to a bird that flees only a short distance.
